subject.title: [Feature]: Support plugin-requestable session isolation for trust boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-requestable quarantined execution as a public Plugin SDK/runtime contract, and what guarantees should sandboxing, tool constraints, and returned trust metadata make?
rationale: This changes a public plugin API and runtime security boundary, and automation cannot safely choose whether the feature should promise OS/process isolation, subagent-only isolation, metadata-only trust signals, or no new core contract.

options.title: Define the isolation contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify the supported isolation level, allowed-tool enforcement, failure behavior, and trust metadata shape before implementation.

options.title: Limit this to existing primitives
options.body: Document sessions_spawn, sandbox:'require', allowAgents, and plugin approval hooks as the supported path without adding a hook-returned isolation directive.

options.title: Reject core-level quarantined execution
options.body: Close this if maintainers decide strong trust isolation must remain an operator/gateway/OS deployment boundary rather than a Plugin SDK runtime feature.

recommendation.title: Define the isolation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify the supported isolation level, allowed-tool enforcement, failure behavior, and trust metadata shape before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans both plugin approval shape and subagent/session security work.
